weights_source: lukewys/laion_clap, music_audioset_epoch_15_esc_90.14.pt (CC0-1.0): the checkpoint the model's makers trained. The Hugging Face release named in "model" holds the same architecture with weights that were never trained; it supplies the layout only. The .onnx file carries the name above in its own metadata (clap_weights).
graph_input: mel: float32 (batch, 3, 1, 1001, 64) — 3 log-mel windows per track
graph_contains: CLAP audio tower + projection + per-clip L2 norm + mean over 3 windows + final L2 norm (mirrors ClapModel.get_audio_features + embed.py pooling)

protocol.decode: librosa.load(path, sr=48000, mono=True); reject < 2 s; zero-pad each window tail to 480000 samples
protocol.pooling: in-graph: mean of the 3 per-clip unit vectors, then renormalize

mel.fft_dtype_roundtrip: rfft result stored complex64, then |.|^2 in float64 (matches transformers audio_utils.py:947)

_distribution.note: clap_music.onnx is not in the git repository: it is 267 MiB, it needed the git-lfs add-on to clone, and it drew on a shared monthly bandwidth allowance. It is published as a release asset and fetched with `python tools/fetch_model.py`, which verifies the sha256 below before putting it in place. The frozen Windows app is unaffected: its installer carries the model inside.
